_provenance.generated_by: Convergence analysis of bootstrap and RAWR CI width as n_replicates increases
_provenance.data_origin: Synthetic data drawn from known distributions. No external data.

_description: How quickly do bootstrap and RAWR confidence intervals converge as the number of replicates increases? Determines the optimal replicate count for a given accuracy target.
_groundspring_question: How many resampling replicates are enough? Wasting compute on excess replicates wastes energy; too few give unreliable intervals. The convergence rate quantifies resampling efficiency.
_cross_spring: All springs — MC methodology optimization from Exp 007

model._description: Run bootstrap and RAWR at geometrically increasing replicate counts (100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000) on Gaussian, log-normal, and heavy-tailed (t-distribution) data. Track CI width convergence.
